npi-1851295646.summary: PureHealth Compounding LLC is a newly registered compounding pharmacy in Harleysville, PA (phone 833-990-7873). The NPI registry lists Daniel Nagrudny as owner and pharmacist-in-charge. I found no website, LinkedIn page, reviews or news for it, so its services and customers are not confirmed.
npi-1851295646.fit: A brand-new compounding pharmacy is in StoneDock's best-fit segment. Its toll-free 833 number suggests it may ship or serve patients remotely, though I couldn't confirm that. It may need a patient app, lab-PDF AI and a medication workflow (payment, prescription, EHR sync, refills) that StoneDock Connect already runs. This is the same model as the live client MyWellness App with the Wellvi pharmacy. The main uncertainty is whether it focuses on GLP-1s, peptides or hormones, or on general compounding.
pain_points: No patient-facing app or digital channel yet, as a new launch
Handling prescription, payment, refill and EHR sync without building its own stack
Retaining patients on recurring compounded therapies such as GLP-1s, peptides and hormones
Showing patient consent and an audit trail for HIPAA and state pharmacy oversight
Competing with established compounders and telehealth partners that already offer an app

sec-2159134.summary: Atmos Clinic is a seed-stage New York City startup, founded in 2026, that is building an AI-native care platform. It has chat-based virtual primary care, an employer-sponsored healthcare expense card, and a marketplace of transparently priced local services. One aggregator says it targets small employers at about $50 per employee per month. That figure came from a search summary and I did not confirm it on a page. The company appears to be pre-launch.
sec-2159134.fit: Atmos Clinic is a well-funded, brand-new telehealth and primary care company with a 1-10 person team. It is hiring a founding product engineer to build its React Native/Expo app. It needs patient-facing health data, AI and consent infrastructure. Connect's FHIR, HIPAA-ready consent and audit, lab-PDF AI and medication workflow could let it launch sooner than building that stack itself. The risk is that it is building its own AI-native platform in-house, and its founders come from Ambience Healthcare and Oscar Health, so they may prefer to build. The $8 per member per month price may also clash with a roughly $50 per employee per month model.
pain_points: A tiny team (1-10 people) has to build a mobile app plus a HIPAA-grade FHIR data layer, consent and audit trail from scratch
Turning labs and records (including PDFs) into AI insights for its chat-based primary care
Prescription, payment, EHR sync and refill workflows for a virtual primary care service
Keeping patients inside its own branded app while it integrates with outside labs, imaging and pharmacies
Margin pressure on a roughly $50 per employee per month model, so a per-member data and AI cost needs to be justified
